chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu Sa'id al-Makari from Abu Basir from al-Harith ibn al-Mughayrah al-Nasri, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (Everything is perishable but Him). He (AS) answered: Everything is perishable except the one who followed the Right Path.

key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: His Face (metaphor for His essence or countenance)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Everything is perishable but Him' mean according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets 'His Face' not merely as God's essence, but as the path of truth and adherence to the Imams, a key Shia hermeneutical approach distinguishing between the perishable creation and the eternal divine reality. This interpretation aligns with the Shia concept of *Wala* (divine affinity) as the anchor of permanence in a transient world, offering believers a practical criterion for salvation beyond mere existence.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar on the authority of Ya`qub ibn Yazid on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Mukari on the authority of Abu Basir on the authority of al-Harith ibn al-Mughayrah al-Nasri that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: Everything is perishable but him. He (AS) answered: “Everything is perishable except the one who followed the Right Path.”
